title: Polaris’s Future Home: What Happens in 3,200 Years

segments.text: Hook: Have you ever wondered who will be the next North Star?
The answer is tied to Earth’s slow wobble, called axial precession, which traces a 26,000‑year cycle.
Over time the north celestial pole moves in a large circle against the stars, so the bright star that sits near the pole today will change.
In about 3,200 years the star Gamma Cephei will become the new marker.
Payoff: This gradual shift means the stars that guide us will keep changing, but the pattern of seasons will stay the same as it has for millennia.
